rows.evidence: chart.js gained fitLabel, documented as shrinking an axis label 'so a long label never leaves the SVG on a narrow screen'. It does not. The x label is centred at margin.left + inner.w/2, so its right half has inner.w/2 + margin.right of room, but fitLabel is given room = inner.w + margin.left - 4 (42 px too much with the default margins). The y label is centred at margin.top + inner.h/2 but given room = height - 8. Probe in Chromium (verify3-L07-L08/scripts/fitlabel_probe.py: a 328 x 220 plot with default margins, labels of 30-80 characters): a 50-character x label (296 px, not shrunk) overflows the right edge by 5.5 px; every shrunk x label (52-80 characters, 11.9 down to 8 px) still overflows by 9-22 px; a 36-character y label (204 px, 12 px, not shrunk) is clipped 8.6 px at the top, and shrunk y labels by 12-71 px, worst at the 8 px floor. No L07 or L08 state triggers it: in every state recorded for this ledger (L07 1,562 + L08 320 at 360 px; L08 also at 414, 600, 768, 1280 px; L07 at 768 and 1280 px) all axis labels render at 12 px and no SVG text leaves its SVG. page_smoke does not test text clipped inside an SVG, so other pages' figures are unprotected.
rows.fix: In fitLabel's callers, give each label the room on its tighter side: x: inner.w + 2 * Math.min(margin.left, margin.right) - 4 (or centre the label on the full SVG width and use width - 8); y: inner.h + 2 * Math.min(margin.top, margin.bottom) - 4 (or centre the rotated label on the full height). When even 8 px does not fit, wrap or truncate with an ellipsis instead of overflowing. Add a page_smoke check that every SVG <text> bounding box lies inside its SVG at 360 px.
